info.title: FBP Protocol 2.0 over Reticulum
info.description:
Machine-readable interface document for FBP Protocol 2.0, the decentralized runtime protocol for peer-to-peer visual programming (NoFlo, MicroFlo) over the Reticulum Network Stack. The normative human-readable reference is `SPEC.md` in the same package; the two documents are kept in lockstep and no wire-format change lands without its counterpart in both.

**License.** This document is dedicated to the public domain under **CC0-1.0** (`SPDX-License-Identifier: CC0-1.0`): anyone may implement, copy, modify, publish, use, and distribute it freely, for any purpose, without conditions or attribution requirements. The reference *implementation* in this package is licensed separately under the EUPL-1.2 (see `LICENSE`). The split is deliberate: unencumbered specs grow ecosystems; the code keeps the project's greenfield license.

**Perspective.** The *application* described by this document is the **runtime**. On every channel, `publish` means the runtime sends and `subscribe` means the runtime receives. Clients (visual programming UIs, monitors) read the document with the directions inverted.

**Wire encoding.** All command frames are flat, positional MessagePack arrays; keyed dictionaries are banned for command framing to preserve radio airtime. The payload schemas below therefore describe fixed-arity arrays, with field types per position. MsgPack maps appear only as open *payload data* (logical clocks, manifest entries, component definitions, event payloads) where the frame shape is heterogeneous. Because AsyncAPI has no native MsgPack or RNS binding, each message carries its wire form as a hex-encoded MsgPack frame in `x-msgpack-hex` and its decoded form in `examples`; the package's test suite decodes every `x-msgpack-hex` example through the real codecs and re-encodes it byte-for-byte, so this document cannot drift from the implementation unnoticed.

**Capability mask.** Reticulum handles authentication (`link.identify()`); the runtime maps the verified identity against its local DACAR capability store and announces the result in the `0x02` handshake. Bits: `0x01` GRAPH_READ, `0x02` GRAPH_EDIT, `0x04` METADATA_SYNC, `0x08` TELEMETRY_READ, `0x10` COMPONENT_READ, `0x20` COMPONENT_WRITE, `0x40` LIFECYCLE_CTRL, `0x80` ADMIN. Each channel declares its requirement in `x-capability`.

**Protocol version.** A single generation integer, currently `2`, advertised in the announce app_data and repeated in the `0x02` handshake. Bumped only on breaking wire changes; additive evolution does not bump it.

rns.description:
Reticulum link transport. Connections are established over RNS Links to a runtime's single-purpose destination, normally discovered by scanning announces. Authentication is delegated entirely to Reticulum's `link.identify()`; no protocol payload carries secrets.

**Announce discovery.** Runtimes announce under a stable destination aspect with app_data `msgpack([ protocol_version, destination_hash_raw16, node_name ])` — see the `announceAppData` message. A scanning client can reject an incompatible announce after decoding a single fixint. The aspect name is not versioned; app_data is the version advertisement.

After `link_established` with a verified identity, the runtime unilaterally sends `0x02 CMD_AUTH_RESPONSE` (channel `cmd/0x02`) carrying the protocol version again, the capability mask, and a limitation code — the in-link truth for stale or cached announces.

cmd/0x02.description: Runtime → client, unilaterally after link establishment with a verified identity.
cmd/0x02.x-capability: none — this message *is* the capability advertisement

cmd/0x10.description: Client → runtime: request graph state synchronization for an epoch.

cmd/0x11.description: Runtime → client: epochs match, no delta transfer needed.

cmd/0x12.description: Runtime → client: the client's epoch is stale; fetch the baseline snapshot via the Reticulum Resource API.

cmd/0x14.description: Bidirectional CRDT graph operation. Client → runtime: graph edits. Runtime → client: runtime-initiated graph changes converge to all connected clients via the op log.
cmd/0x14.x-capability: GRAPH_EDIT (0x02) for client-sent mutations; runtime-initiated updates need no client capability

cmd/0x20.description: Client → runtime: registry sync request against the client's known registry hash (Two-Step Cache, step 1).

cmd/0x22.description: Runtime → client: registry manifest (Two-Step Cache, step 1 response). Entries are valid with a signature and no source; each carries the declared component kind.

cmd/0x23.description: Client → runtime: request details for unknown components only (Two-Step Cache, step 2).

cmd/0x24.description: Runtime → client: component definitions. Succeeds for stubs, answering from the signature; the declared kind travels with every component.

cmd/0x25.description: Client → runtime: atomic full-source component update. Sources over 500 bytes SHOULD travel as a Reticulum Resource hash instead of a raw string.

cmd/0x27.description: Client → runtime: dynamic ES module install via HTTP, npm, or RNS. Third-party libraries MUST be EUPL-1.2-compatible. The URI resolves through the ecosystem catalog's npm/JSR/version/hash provenance fields.

cmd/0x30.description: Client → runtime: subscribe to a telemetry stream. The flush interval is a request; the runtime's actual flush cadence is its physical-policy decision.

cmd/0x32.description: Runtime → client: buffered, delta-encoded flowtrace chunk for a subscription.

lxmf/fbp.telemetry.description: Runtime → mesh, over LXMF store-and-forward (not a link channel): asynchronous telemetry drops, event-driven or scheduled opportunistically with randomized jitter to respect Proof-of-Work limits. LXMF app name: `fbp.telemetry`.
lxmf/fbp.telemetry.x-capability: none — authenticated by the LXMF transport itself

ComponentKind.description: The shared component-kind vocabulary: publish-time manifests, loader sidecars, manifest entries, and details all use this one enum. Declared data — never inferred from absence of source.

Port.description: One port of a component signature. Field names follow the FBP runtime convention; the publish-time manifest's `name` maps onto `id`. Absent optional fields are omitted from the wire to save airtime.

ComponentDetail.description: A component definition as carried by `0x24`. Valid with no implementation behind it (stubs).

announceAppData.name: announceAppData
announceAppData.title: RNS announce app_data
announceAppData.summary: Version advertisement and connection coordinates carried in the runtime's RNS announce payload.
announceAppData.description: Not a link frame: this is the app_data of the runtime's RNS announce under its stable destination aspect. `protocol_version` comes first so a scanner can reject an incompatible announce after decoding a single fixint; `destination_hash_raw16` is the raw 16-byte destination hash; `node_name` is a MsgPack string. The whole payload stays far under the 128-byte announce app_data limit.

authResponse.name: authResponse
authResponse.title: 0x02 CMD_AUTH_RESPONSE
authResponse.summary: Capability advertisement sent unilaterally after link establishment with a verified identity.

items.description: protocol_version — the in-link truth for stale or cached announces
capability_mask — bitwise CAPABILITY: 0x01 GRAPH_READ, 0x02 GRAPH_EDIT, 0x04 METADATA_SYNC, 0x08 TELEMETRY_READ, 0x10 COMPONENT_READ, 0x20 COMPONENT_WRITE, 0x40 LIFECYCLE_CTRL, 0x80 ADMIN
limitation_code — 0x00 full access, 0x01 hardware constrained, 0x02 permission denied, 0x03 link saturated, 0x04 concurrency lock

crdtSyncReq.name: crdtSyncReq
crdtSyncReq.title: 0x10 CMD_CRDT_SYNC_REQ
crdtSyncReq.summary: Client requests graph state synchronization for an epoch.

items.description: client_clocks — map of client id to that client's logical clock

crdtUpToDate.name: crdtUpToDate
crdtUpToDate.title: 0x11 CMD_CRDT_UP_TO_DATE
crdtUpToDate.summary: Epochs match; no delta transfer needed.

crdtStaleEpoch.name: crdtStaleEpoch
crdtStaleEpoch.title: 0x12 CMD_CRDT_STALE_EPOCH
crdtStaleEpoch.summary: The client's epoch is stale; fetch the baseline snapshot via the Reticulum Resource API.

items.description: rns_resource_hash — where to fetch the baseline snapshot

crdtUpdate.name: crdtUpdate
crdtUpdate.title: 0x14 CMD_CRDT_UPDATE
crdtUpdate.summary: Positional CRDT graph operation, flowing both directions.
crdtUpdate.description: The op taxonomy is a mapped projection of the changeset reference model owned by the noflo-ui materialization work: insert node `0x01`, insert edge `0x02`, insert IIP `0x03`, tombstone `0x04`, UI metadata `0x05` (dropped by constrained nodes). Modify is encoded as tombstone + insert at the wire level — an encoding detail, never the semantic unit.

items.description: op_type — 0x01 insert node, 0x02 insert edge, 0x03 insert IIP, 0x04 tombstone, 0x05 UI metadata
entity_id — the graph entity the operation addresses
payload — entity definition for inserts, tombstoned entity reference for removals, metadata map for UI metadata ops

compSyncReq.name: compSyncReq
compSyncReq.title: 0x20 CMD_COMP_SYNC_REQ
compSyncReq.summary: Client requests registry sync against its known registry hash.

compManifest.name: compManifest
compManifest.title: 0x22 CMD_COMP_MANIFEST
compManifest.summary: Registry manifest of the Two-Step Cache, step 1 response.
compManifest.description: Each entry is the positional `[sig_hash, kind]` tuple: the manifest carries the declared component kind and is valid with a signature and no source. `sig_hash` is the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical signature serialization (sorted-key JSON over the kind and the full port field set), so a client matching a hash skips the details round-trip.

items.description: sig_hash — SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical signature

compDetailReq.name: compDetailReq
compDetailReq.title: 0x23 CMD_COMP_DETAIL_REQ
compDetailReq.summary: Client requests details for the components it does not already know.

compDetailRes.name: compDetailRes
compDetailRes.title: 0x24 CMD_COMP_DETAIL_RES
compDetailRes.summary: Component definitions with their declared kinds; succeeds for stubs.

compWrite.name: compWrite
compWrite.title: 0x25 CMD_COMP_WRITE
compWrite.description: For sources over 500 bytes, clients SHOULD pass a Reticulum Resource hash instead of a raw string. A write to a previously stub-only entry implements it while the signature stays unchanged — source and signature are orthogonal.

items.description: source — full source string or RNS resource hash
package_uri — HTTP, npm, or RNS; resolves through the ecosystem catalog's provenance fields

pubsubSub.name: pubsubSub
pubsubSub.title: 0x30 CMD_PUBSUB_SUB
pubsubSub.summary: Subscribe to a telemetry stream with a client-requested flush interval.

items.description: target_type — what is subscribed to (e.g. a graph or network)
requested_flush_interval_ms — a request; the runtime's flush cadence is its physical-policy decision

flowtraceChunk.name: flowtraceChunk
flowtraceChunk.title: 0x32 CMD_FLOWTRACE_CHUNK
flowtraceChunk.description: Event storms never hit the wire raw: events buffer into chunks, each event carrying a uint32 millisecond delta from the chunk's base timestamp. Event types: `0x01` DATA (raw value), `0x02` BEGIN_GROUP / `0x03` END_GROUP (group string), `0x04` ERROR (exception string), `0x05` CONSOLE (`[stream_id, log_string]`), `0x06` LIFECYCLE (transition code: `0x01` start, `0x02` stop, `0x03` safe-mode, `0x04` failed transition — a rejected `start()` leaves the runtime an honest message to send, with the detail in an accompanying `0x04` ERROR event), `0x07` VISUAL_STATE (`[format_type, binary_pixels]`).

items.description: base_timestamp_ms — epoch milliseconds of delta zero

lxmTelemetry.name: lxmTelemetry
lxmTelemetry.title: LXMF store-and-forward telemetry payload
lxmTelemetry.summary: Flat telemetry array dispatched to the mesh via LXMF app `fbp.telemetry`.
lxmTelemetry.description: Not a link frame: the payload of an LXMF drop for asynchronous monitoring. Drops are event-driven (e.g. fault conditions) or scheduled opportunistically during peak solar-generation hours with randomized jitter, to respect Proof-of-Work limits on microcontrollers.

items.description: timestamp — epoch milliseconds of the snapshot
device metrics; any value may be null when unmeasurable
visual_format — 0x01 FontAwesome, 0x02 P4 Netpbm 84x84 monochrome, 0x03 P6 Netpbm 18x18 RGB
errors — fault conditions recorded since the last drop

traceFile.name: traceFile
traceFile.title: Streamable trace file
traceFile.summary: Self-contained, append-only flowtrace recording for playback in UI Web Workers.
traceFile.description: Not a link frame: a file format. Frame 1 is the topology snapshot `[0xF0, format_ver, timestamp_ms, runtime_metadata, complete_graph_definition]` and must come first; frames 2..N are raw `0x32 CMD_FLOWTRACE_CHUNK` byte arrays appended sequentially as they flush from the engine. Frames are self-delimiting MsgPack values, so a recording can be parsed incrementally — including while it is still being written.
